svg.text: How a role's system prompt is assembled
Scope · 15 built-in parts, 3 team sections, 2 bundled Source skills · composePrompt() joins the parts with blank lines
In what order are the parts joined?
Top to bottom is the order promptParts() returns. Rows 8 and 11 are for the main Session only.
A role's prompt, part by part
runtime/shared, then the role's own runtime/orchestrator or runtime/worker
dispatch for the main Session, or work for a worker
admission — main Session only, dropped for a worker
environment (generated again for each model request)
policy — main Session only, generated, always last
Unmarked rows are fixed text both roles read; a worker's own prompt skips rows 8 and 11.
Which text does a built-in part use?
builtIn() reads the team's saved override only when one exists for that part.
Which Source skills does a Session get?
github is always registered; feishu only when a Feishu bot is configured.
only if a Feishu bot is set up
registered in the Session's skill scope
Simplified: a worker's prompt has no admission or policy section at all, not an empty one (src/app/prompts.ts:111,114).
Not shown: a part with empty text, such as an empty team section, is left out (src/app/prompts.ts:115).
Not shown: the composed prompt gets a revision header and, for a live Ticket, a trailing mandate note (src/app/sessions.ts:248).
